newsitem.title: USA: China feed-grain import needs soar - US trade group.
newsitem.headline: China feed-grain import needs soar - US trade group.

text.p: China will import huge quantities of feed (coarse) grains in the coming decade, beginning with a hefty upturn in imports in 1997/98, the U.S. Feed Grains Council forecast Tuesday.
In an annual report, the council said China would have net imports of 1.5 million tonnes in the current marketing year, leaping to 4.255 million in 1997/98 and doubling the next year.
"Net feed grain imports are projected to grow to over 23 million tonnes in 2005, an average 36 percent annual growth rate over the next nine years," the forecast said.
"Its (China's) enormous enormous growth in domestic demand likely will require greater and greater imports in the future," the council said.

Growth in the livestock sector, fueled by higher incomes and burgeoning tastes for meats and dairy products, has been a major factor in a continued flow of feed grains into China despite sharp upturns in domestic production, it said.

China made a splash in the corn market recently by selling corn for export. U.S. Agriculture Department has forecast China to export 500,000 tonnes in 1996/97, about the same as imports, but has not updated its forecasts since the sales.
